source_citation: Oke, Pilo, Ridgway, Kiss and Rykova (2019), A search for the Tasman Front, Journal of Marine Systems 199, 103217, doi:10.1016/j.jmarsys.2019.103217.
source_locator: Publisher-indexed abstract and Introduction; author repository abstract. Historical comparison: Tilburg et al. (2001), Introduction, journal p. 2918, Figure 2 caption p. 2919.
source_access: Oke et al. publisher-indexed abstract and Introduction and ANU repository abstract read. Direct publisher and author PDF retrieval failed; full 2019 article not inspected. Tilburg et al. author-hosted original PDF Introduction and Figure 2 caption read. No figure, velocity field or temperature section digitized.
scope: Historical composite frontal pathway compared with a reassessment of central Tasman Sea continuity. Named inventory entry retained; no single instantaneous axis or whole-current endpoints admitted.
layer: Historical infrared/front locations and climatological steric height relative to 2000 m are different diagnostic supports. Neither establishes a uniform-depth current axis or velocity-defined width.
time_convention: Unsynchronized historical source sets and climatological interpretation remain separate from instantaneous and seasonal geometries.

historical_composite.citation: Tilburg, Hurlburt, O’Brien and Shriver (2001), The Dynamics of the East Australian Current System: The Tasman Front, the East Auckland Current, and the East Cape Current, JPO 31, 2917–2943.

source_sets.original_source: Mulhearn (1987), as described by Tilburg et al. (2001)
source_sets.duration_resolution: Unresolved printed duration/date-span discrepancy; do not reinterpret 29 months as continuous coverage.

source_sets.original_source: Stanton (1979), as described by Tilburg et al. (2001)

continuity_assessment.source_convention: Oke et al. (2019), indexed Introduction: CARS 2009 steric-height climatology, relative to 2000 m.
continuity_assessment.interpretation: Time averaging can smear changing pathways; a persistent narrow coherent jet cannot be assumed from the mean. The reassessment also considers discontinuous streams and eddies.

name_equivalence_status: Eastern extension of the EAC is a naming proposal in Oke et al. (2019); no automatic alias, new released identity or relation admitted.
remaining_gates: Define the target as a historical composite, a dated jet, a mean-flow connection or a transport corridor before measuring it.
Inspect original satellite/cruise sources and resolve the printed 29-month/date-span discrepancy; retain unsynchronized coverage and the 164–166 E gap.
Use compatible velocity fields to diagnose any current axis; classify interrupted or multiple branches rather than forcing one connecting polyline.
Keep East Australian coastal reach and New Zealand boundary currents separate; review any naming equivalence explicitly.
Recover matching dated transverse boundaries and repeated comparable seasonal samples before width or annual ranges.
